rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular call is ascribed to the Messenger because the call is one: God's call appears through him, and his call is not distinct from God's.
rows.anchor: Zira davet birdir. Allah’ın daveti Resûlünden zâhir olacak ve Resûlün daveti Allah’ın davetinden başka bir şey olmayacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life-giving call is to knowledge or action that lifts people from an inanimate or animal state toward free, happy, eternal human life.
rows.anchor: cemâdât ve behâim hâlinden çıkarıp insanlığın namzed olduğu muhtâr, mes‘ud, ebedî hayâta hürriyetinizle yükseltecek bir ilim veya amel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to summon people to this life, and hearing the call requires an immediate, eager response while they still have the opportunity.
rows.anchor: Peygamber buna davet için ba‘s edilmiş ve insanlara kulak, dil ve akl ü irade bunun için verilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to and more sovereign over a person than the person's own heart; He knows its contents and controls them.
rows.anchor: Ona kalbinden, kalbine ondan daha yakın, daha hâkimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can frustrate ambitions, change intentions, convictions, and tastes, turn a person against himself, remove reason and consciousness, and finally take life.
rows.anchor: Azimlerini bozuverir, niyetlerini tahvil ediverir; kanaatlerini, zevklerini değiştiriverir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people cannot resist when God separates them from their hearts or summons them to death, they must answer the life-giving call before that moment.
rows.anchor: Allah sizinle kalbiniz arasına perde çektiği ve ölüme davet ettiği vakit icâbet etmemeye ve cebrine mukāvemet eylemeye imkân bulamazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people will be gathered to God alone and recompensed according to the rank of their deeds, so they should not excuse disobedience by appealing to the loss of heart or life.
rows.anchor: Başkasına değil yalnız Allah’a toplanacaksınız da amellerinizin mertebesine göre cezâsını çekeceksiniz.

words: لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنكُمْ خَآصَّةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A communal trial will not strike only the wrongdoers who caused it; its harm can spread to the whole community, including the innocent.
rows.anchor: her hâlde içinizden bilhassa zulmedenlere isabet etmez. Yalnız işi yerinden oynatanlara mahsus bir musibet olmakla kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some sins have public consequences: publicizing evil, neglecting enjoining right and forbidding wrong, corrupting belief, factional division, and laxity in jihad.
rows.anchor: i‘lân-ı münker, emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münkerde müdâhene, ifsâd-ı akide, iftirâk-ı kelime, cihadda tekâsül bu kabildendir.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith compares communal harm to a person drilling a hole in a ship: the resulting drowning afflicts everyone aboard, not only the culprit and those who assist or stay silent.
rows.anchor: Hadîs-i nebevîde vârid olduğu üzere bir geminin dibini delmeye uğraşan bir şahsın fiili öyle bir gark musibetini intac eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preventing such harm and stopping the hole-maker is a collective duty: if some perform it, all are saved; if all neglect it, all suffer.
rows.anchor: bu vazifeyi îfâ ettikleri surette hepsi kurtulur, hiçbiri aldırmayıp gemi delindiği surette ise hepsi musâb olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intervention must preserve balance; trying to stop wrongdoing must not itself cause upheaval that overturns the community's ship.
rows.anchor: gemiyi delmeye kalkanı men‘edelim derken herc ü merc ile muvazeneyi bozup geminin devrilmesine de sebebiyet vermemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prescribes public vigilance, personal self-examination, orderly and courteous oversight, and commitment to obedience to God and the Messenger to prevent communal discord.
rows.anchor: herkes kendi nefsini muhasebe etmek, sâlisen cereyân-ı umûmîden gaflet etmeyerek murâkabe-i umûmiyeyi dikkat ve intizam ve hüsn-i ahlâk ile idâme eylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects this communal responsibility with the community that calls to good, commands right, and forbids wrong in 3:104.
rows.anchor: وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General tribulation is punishment both for the original wrongdoers and for negligent bystanders who allowed the wrongdoing to take hold.
rows.anchor: fitne-i âmme yalnız asıl cürmü îkā‘eden zâlimlerin cezâsı değil, aynı zamanda korunmayıp onun îkā‘ına meydan veren gāfillerin gafletlerinin de cezâsıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who strive until their last breath but do not succeed are excused before God, as expressed in 7:164.
rows.anchor: Son nefese kadar çalışıp da muvaffak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the excused may share worldly suffering through proximity to wrongdoers; their hardship can increase the punishment of those responsible.
rows.anchor: dünyada o musîbet-i âmmenin dâire-i şümûlünden hâriç kalmamaları da muhtemil bulunuyor. Âhirette me’cur olurlarsa da dünyada mihnet çekerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment is severe enough to overtake wrongdoers' surroundings and neighbors as well as the wrongdoers themselves.
rows.anchor: İkābının şiddetindendir ki yalnız zâlimlere münhasır kalmaz da onların muhitlerini, mücâvirlerini de istîlâ eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning itself shows how life-giving the Messenger's call is and reinforces the command to answer it.
rows.anchor: İmdi bunları böyle bildirip de وَٱتَّقُوا۟ emrini tebliğ eden Resûl’ün ne kadar ihyâkâr bir davette bulunduğunu anlayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers had been few and oppressed in the land, in Mecca under Quraysh or under Persian and Roman power.
rows.anchor: Mekke arzında Kureyş’in veya Fürs ü Rumun elleri altında makhurdunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hostile people around them made the believers fear being seized and crushed; they lacked security and peace.
rows.anchor: Etraftaki halk bu kadar nazar-ı husûmetle bakıyordu, emniyet ü âsâyiş yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God settled the believers in Medina after their migration and granted them security and peace.
rows.anchor: Allah sizi yerleştirdi Medine’ye nakl ü iskân edip emniyet ü âsâyiş verdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened them through the Ansar, angelic aid, and victory at Badr.
rows.anchor: Ensar’ın muzâhereti, melâikenin imdâdı ve Bedir zaferiyle kuvvetlendirip o küffâra karşı müeyyed kıldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provided lawful blessings, including spoils, and moved the believers from abasement to a life of honor; they should give thanks.
rows.anchor: helâl nimetlerden sizi merzuk da etti ganimetler nasip eyledi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ghanm can mean acquiring something without toil or obtaining satisfaction from an enemy; it also names the acquisition itself.
rows.anchor: “Gunm”, esasen bir şeye renc ü meşakkatsiz nâil olmak veya düşmandan doyumluk almak mânalarına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In law, ghanima is property taken from unbelievers by force in war; property acquired by treaty is fay', so ghanima is narrower than fay'.
rows.anchor: Şeriatta ise “ganimet” küffârdan anveten, yani harben alınan maldır. Binâen‘aleyh velevse harbin neticesi olsun bir sulh ve ahd ile alınan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling covers every item of booty, however small, even a needle or thread.
rows.anchor: aldığınız ganimet ne şeyden olursa olsun velevse bir iğne veya iplik bulunsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole belongs initially to God under 8:1; one fifth is set aside and divided into five shares for God, the Messenger, kin, orphans, the poor, and travelers: one share to the Messenger and four to the other groups.
rows.anchor: humusu, beşte biri sırf Allah içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All spoils are entrusted to the fighters for expenditure under God's law and in the public interest; the law nevertheless preserves their private benefit by reserving only one fifth for public uses.
rows.anchor: Evvelemirde enfâl ve ganâimin hepsi Allah’ındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining four fifths belong to the fighters; if they claim them, distribution is obligatory, but each may voluntarily relinquish any amount for God before or after distribution.
rows.anchor: Ganimetin humustan bâkī kalan beşte dördüne gelince onu da size, siz gāzilere bırakır. Şu hâlde gāziler dilerlerse haklarını ister, taksîmi vâcib olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet's death, disposition of his share of the fifth is a matter for juristic reasoning; details belong to fiqh.
rows.anchor: sonra onun humustan sehmi de müctehedün fîhtir ve bu cihetlerin tafsîli fıkha aittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two reports place the verse's revelation either at Badr or at the Banu Qaynuqa expedition, one month and three days after Badr.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin Bedir’de veya Bedir’den bir ay üç gün sonra Benî Kaynuka Gazvesi’nde nâzil olduğu hakkında iki rivayet vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Furqan day is Badr, when Muslims and unbelievers clashed; what God sent to the Prophet included revelation, angels, and aid.
rows.anchor: hakk u bâtılın ayrıldığı Bedir günü kulumuza indirdiğimiz şeylere -vahiy ve melâike ve nusrete- iman etmiş hakīkī mü’minler iseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badr's victory of a small, weak force over a larger, stronger one demonstrates God's power; following His command can bring further gifts.
rows.anchor: o günkü gibi çoğa karşı aza, kavîye karşı zayıfa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers were on the near bank in a poor position, while the enemy held the more favorable far bank; the caravan was below them by the shore.
rows.anchor: siz vâdinin beri kıyısında -fena bir mevki‘de- idiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan was below and under the Muslims' threat, but its presence could embolden the enemy and unsettle the Muslims; overall military conditions favored the enemy.
rows.anchor: bunlar düşman ordusunun sizi işgal edecek ve aynı zamanda harbe hırslarını tahrik edecek bir kuvveti ve bu vaziyet sizi korkutacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the armies agreed on a meeting after recognizing the imbalance, the Muslims would have lost courage, broken the appointment, and avoided the fight; human planning alone could not have produced this victory.
rows.anchor: bu vaziyete gelince cesaret edemez, vaadinizde hulf eder, zaferden me’yus olurdunuz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a prior appointment and without leaving them to themselves, God brought the two sides together to enact His decree, distinguish truth from falsehood and allies from enemies, and establish His promised aid as decisive proof.
rows.anchor: Allah o fiile çıkan emri o hârikulâde emr-i vâki‘i; o vaziyeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badr was a visible sign and proof: those who opposed God and His Messenger perished or would perish, while obedient believers gained or would gain material or spiritual life and salvation.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın öyle bir âyet-i vâzıhası ve öyle bir beyyine-i meşhûdesidir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this manifest proof, neither the dead nor living, unbeliever nor believer, can present an argument or excuse against God.
rows.anchor: ne ölünün ne dirinin, ne kâfirin ne mü’minin Allah’a karşı ne ibraz edebilecek bir hücceti ne de serd edebilecek bir mazereti yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what His friends and enemies say, knows their intentions, beliefs, aims, and secrets, and knows what He will do concerning them.
rows.anchor: Dostlarının düşmanlarının söylediklerini işitir, niyet ve itikadlarını, maksat ve muzmerlerini ve haklarında ne yapacağını bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing phrase reinforces the ending of 8:17 and directs attention back to it.
rows.anchor: فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extraordinary events and miracles are not products of chance.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı havârik ve mu‘cizât bir eser-i tesadüf değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the Prophet's menām as his dream, sleep, bed, or eyes, and says the dream links the beginning and end of the event in consciousness, showing it was no coincidence.
rows.anchor: az gösteriyordu bu işle alâkadar olmak üzere evvelâ bir rüya gösteriyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed the Prophet the enemy as few, and he told and encouraged his companions, steadying them; this was a wise and genuinely beneficial measure, not deception.
rows.anchor: Sâniyen O, çokluğu az gösteriyordu, sen de bunu haber verip ashâbını teşcî‘ve tesbit ediyordun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had God shown the enemy as numerous, the Muslims would have lost heart and disputed over whether to stand firm or flee.
rows.anchor: harb hususunda re’ylerinize tefrika düşecek, kiminiz sebat kiminiz firar taraftarı olacaktınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected them by showing the enemy's true insignificance rather than its apparent numbers, preventing fear and dispute and bringing them safely to their goal.
rows.anchor: sana rüyanda onların zâhirdeki kesretlerini değil, hakikatteki kıymetsizliklerini gösterdi, sizi yıldırmadı ve nizâ‘a meydan vermedi de sâlim tuttu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the secrets of hearts, what is in people, what will happen, and the causes and conditions by which their states will change.
rows.anchor: Onlarda ne var, ne olacak ve ne gibi esbâb ve şerâit ile hâlleri değişecek, hepsini tamamen bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the coming Day, no one will speak without God's permission.
rows.anchor: meğer ki O’nun izniyle ola yani Allah’ın izniyle söyleyecek olanlar müstesnâ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites 78:38, which likewise limits speech to those permitted by the Merciful.
rows.anchor: لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission does not apply at every station: 77:35–36 describes a station when all are silent and none may speak even to offer an excuse.
rows.anchor: هَٰذَا يَوْمُ لَا يَنطِقُونَ وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies those not allowed to speak as wretched and disgraced, while those permitted to speak are fortunate and blissful.
rows.anchor: Hiç söyletilmeyenler bedbaht, sefil; söze me’zun olanlar bahtiyar, mes‘uddur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In medical terminology, zafīr means inhaling and shahīq means exhaling.
rows.anchor: Etıbbâ ıstılâhında “zefîr” nefes almak, “şehîk” vermektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the original lexical sense, zafīr is drawing breath in deeply and then letting it out, like a distressed person's sigh.
rows.anchor: asl-ı lügatta “zefîr” soluğu uzun uzadıya içeri çektikten sonra dışarı vermektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīq is a sob while crying, caused by intense grief; children's crying can sound this way.
rows.anchor: “Şehîk” de ağlarken hıçkırmaktır ki fazla teessürden neş’et eder. Ve çocukların ağlaması öyle olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening and ending of a donkey's bray are also called zafīr and shahīq respectively, one inhalation and one exhalation.
rows.anchor: eşeğin anırmasının evveline “zefîr”, âhirine “şehîk” denilir ki biri idhâl biri ihrâcdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary Arabic usage these are not ordinary breaths but breathing out and in with a sound of distress.
rows.anchor: “zefîr” ve “şehîk” alelâde nefes alıp verme değil, ıztıraplı bir sesle nefes verip almadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forms of zafīr and shahīq intensify the horror: these are ghastly, unprecedented gasps and sobs.
rows.anchor: “zefîr ve şehîk”teki tenvinler tenkir ve tehvil içindir ki şu demek olur: Fecî bir soluk verip almaları, solurken göğüs geçirip hıçkırmaları vardır

rows.speaker: حسن
rows.claim: A meaning transmitted from Hasan takes zafīr as the rising blaze of Hell, which swells until its inhabitants seem near the top before angels strike them back down.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan naklolunan bir mânaya göre “zefîr” leheb-i cehennemin irtifâ‘ıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He relates the attempted escape and forced return to 32:20, where those trying to leave Hell are sent back into it.
rows.anchor: كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓا۟ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَآ أُعِيدُوا۟ فِيهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Hasan's reading, the fire's swelling and rising is zafīr, and its plunging back down is shahīq; the damned repeatedly rise and fall within it.
rows.anchor: nâr-ı cehennemin köpürüp kabarmasıyla irtifâ‘ları zefîr, inhitatları şehîktir. Ateş içinde böyle çıkıp inip duracaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'as long as the heavens and earth endure' raises the familiar objection that it seems to limit duration and conflict with other statements of eternity.
rows.anchor: Bu kayıtta bir tevkīt şaibesi yok mu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known answer treats such Arabic expressions as idioms for eternity, but Elmalılı says that this still leaves open whether the eternity is only customary and may not settle the dispute.
rows.anchor: lisân-ı Arabda ما أقام ثبير، ما لاح كوكب، ما اختلف الليل والنهار، ما طما البحر vesâire gibi te’bîdden kinaye olduğu beyânıyla cevap da şöhret bulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage concerns the afterlife, these are the afterlife's heavens and earth, not the world's; they have no finite term, so the wording means true endless eternity, confirmed by the next verse's unbroken gift.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki bu âyetlerde ecel-i ma‘dûdun hitâmıyla gelecek olan kıyamet gününden ve bunu tâkip edecek olan ahvâl-i âhiretten bahsedilmekte olduğu için

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that the heavens and earth return to their source of light in the afterlife and remain forever in the light of the Throne.
rows.anchor: Bir de İbn Abbas Hazretleri’nden menkuldür ki semâvât ve arz âhirette me’hazları olan nûra reddedilecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The endless duration should not be mistaken for a self-necessary natural persistence that would make God's judgment and disposal impossible.
rows.anchor: bu nâmütenâhî devam ve hulûd, Allah teâlâ’nın artık hükm ü tasarrufu mümkin olmayacak surette vücûb-i zâtî ile vâcib bir devâm-ı tabîî tevehhüm olunmamak için
